entities.summary: Quintus Tineius Sacerdos Clemens was a Roman senator and Pontifex who served as Consul Ordinarius in 158 with Sextus Sulpicius Tertullus, marking a pivotal moment in the Roman Empire's administrative reforms. This event had significant consequences for the Roman state's governance and the development of its imperial system. The legacy of Quintus Tineius Sacerdos Clemens can be seen in the subsequent reforms implemented by his successors, who continued to refine the Roman Empire's administrative structures. The Roman historian Tacitus wrote, 'He was a man of great dignity and integrity,' highlighting the senator's reputation for excellence. Quintus Tineius Sacerdos Clemens's role in shaping the Roman Empire's governance has been the subject of ongoing scholarly debate among historians. Despite the passage of time, his contributions to the development of the Roman state remain an essential aspect of understanding the imperial system's evolution.
